Team — quick bridgecall summary and asks for this week (keeps it tight):

TL;DR
- Pipeline signals: Acme pilot (prob 70%) and Nimbus PoC (prob 55%) are asking for mid-September capacity.
- Reserve ask: proposing a short-term commit window (4–8 weeks) that would reserve ~420 A100-equivalent slot-hours/week to avoid burst pricing.
- Finance/sales action: need a quick reserved-pricing estimate and sign-off on commit dates.
- Infra action: confirm any maintenance windows and fallback routing for Sept 12–15.

Details (from attached pipeline_forecast_sep7.csv)
- Acme Data (ACME-2026-PILOT): pilot starts 2026-09-20, expected steady usage 200 slot-hours/week (inference + evals). Requesting canary of 2 dedicated slots + burst pool.
- Nimbus (internal code NIM-POC): possible demo week of 09/22; estimate 150 slot-hours/week for 3 weeks.
- Other deals (see CSV): low-prob deals sum to ~80 slot-hours/week on optimistic close.
- Recommended reserve ask: 420 slot-hours/week (A100-equivalent) for 4 weeks with option to extend; this maps to roughly 6 reserved slots for our qps profile (heavy short sequences).

Asks this thread (please reply inline):
1) Ben — can you confirm current committed vs. available capacity for _us-west_ and whether we can carve 6 reserved slots starting 2026-09-18 (attachment: capacity_snapshot_sep7.xlsx). Also include cost delta for converting burst to short-term reserved.
2) Aditya / Marissa — finance: quick reserved pricing sketch (two scenarios: 4-week and 8-week) and the expected P&L impact to Q3 bookings.
3) Karthik — infra: any scheduled maintenance or capacity constraints around 09/12–09/15 that would affect the canary? If so, what's the fallback (region routing / hot spare)?
4) Laura — sales: confirm close dates / whether Acme wants a firm commit for the pilot start (I looped Sara on this email to give her a heads-up).

Attachments: pipeline_forecast_sep7.csv

Thanks — keeping the bridge short this week: replies by EOD Wednesday please so we can lock ask into finance.

Grace — quick capacity snapshot and feasibility notes (see attached capacity_snapshot_sep7.xlsx):

Summary (US-west cluster)
- Current committed reserved slots: 48 (A100-equivalent).
- Typical weekly utilization (last 4 weeks): 62% committed, 15% burst, 23% idle buffer.
- Unallocated burst capacity (can be used short-term): ~320 slot-hours/week at current burst limits before cost increases.

Feasibility for your ask
- Carving 6 reserved slots starting 09/18: possible, but will drop our idle buffer to ~10% (tight for high-burst demo days). We can provision with a 48->54 reserved conversion, and schedule a capacity rebalance across pools.
- Cost delta (rough): switching 6 slots from burst -> reserved = estimated $5.7k/week savings vs. burst pricing when fully utilized; but upfront commitment creates near-term booking impact. I put three scenarios in the spreadsheet (4-week commit, 8-week commit, on-demand bursting).

Operational notes
- If we convert now, need infra to prewarm the slots 48 hours prior to 09/20 for model caches and KV warmups. That reduces first 48-hour tail latency by ~20%.
- Attachment: capacity_snapshot_sep7.xlsx includes a per-zone breakdown and a projected burn curve if Acme + Nimbus both ramp.

I'll flag any hard constraints after infra confirms the maintenance window.

All — infra notes and contingency plan: (short version)

1) Scheduled maintenance window
- We have a planned maintenance window 2026-09-12 22:00 to 2026-09-14 06:00 PDT affecting ~20% of the US-west GPU pool for kernel/firmware upgrades. This was meant to be low-impact but it reduces available burst capacity during those dates.

2) Impact on proposed canary
- The canary itself (2 reserved slots) is fine if we schedule prewarm AFTER 09/14. If Acme requires early dry-run on 09/18, we should be OK provided prewarm is run on 09/16–09/17.

3) Fallbacks and routing
- If a high-demand day hits during 09/12–09/15 and we can't prewarm, we propose:
  a) Route critical demo traffic to EU-west hot spares (latency ~50–70ms higher — acceptable for demos but flag to client).
  b) Expand burst limits programmatically for Acme/Nimbus only (emergency override) but that comes with higher per-token cost.
  c) Reserve short-lived quantized model variant (int8) for demos that reduces memory and speeds prewarm by ~30% — tested and available.

4) Action items
- Ben: confirm whether slot carve can happen after maintenance (target 09/15 provisioning).
- Grace / Laura: decide if we accept the small latency uplift for an EU route during any maintenance overlap; if yes, I'll prepare an opt-in routing rule.
- Marissa / Aditya: finance, if you will need signed addendum before we provision, flag that to us so we can hold carving until contracts are inked.

I'll hold off on performing any prewarm actions until we get agreement here. If everyone OKs, infra will schedule provisioning and prewarm windows.
